Bottleneck.description: A node that limits the graph.

limited_by.description:
What holds the node back: `"destination"` when most of its busy time
is spent waiting for the system it writes to, so that neither more
CPU nor moving it helps; `"work"` otherwise.

waiting.description: Part of that ratio spent waiting for an external system to answer.

kv.description: KV statistics, when the embedding process provides them.

placement.description: Current placement (empty, version 0, when none was published).

deleting.description: Always `true`: workers stop the graph, then its state is removed.

DesiredState.description: What operators want a graph to do.

paused_nodes.description:
Nodes paused individually. A paused node stops consuming its inputs;
backpressure then stalls everything upstream of it.

state.description: Run state of the whole graph.

updated_ms.description: When this document was last changed.

Duration.description: A duration: a number followed by `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h` or `d` (`"5m"`), or a number of milliseconds.

EmittedWindow.description: How far the emitting half of an aggregate node got.

complete.description: Whether every element of the window is out.

error.description: What went wrong, for a person.

bottleneck.description: What limits the graph, if anything.

watermark_ms.description: Minimum watermark of the source slices; null if any is unknown.

GraphId.description: A graph id: 1 to 128 letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

GraphPlan.description: How a graph is cut into slices, computed by the controller.

closed.description:
Retired slices whose state has been deleted. Their log stays closed
to the plans of that time.

closing.description:
Retired slices whose log has been closed, everything they committed
being emitted, with the instant it was: their state is deleted once
no write issued before that can still land.

error.description: Why the graph cannot be planned (unknown operator, unreachable source, ...).

generation.description:
Incremented every time the set of slices changes, as when a source
gains or loses partitions. Slice instances and commit records carry
it: nothing is written under a plan older than what the log holds.

joined.description:
Slices that entered the plan after the graph had started, with the
generation at which they did: the pipeline may have emitted windows
without them, which they must then take for closed.

partitions.description: Partition count of every source node.

retired.description:
Slices that are no longer run, their partition being gone, but whose
committed state still has to be emitted.

spec_version.description: Version of the description this plan was computed from.

GraphSettings.description: Engine settings of a graph. Every field has a default.

chunk_size.description: Number of records per chunk on an edge.

flush_interval.description: How often closed windows are looked for.

gc_grace.description:
How long the index entry of an emitted window outlives its state. A
store command issued by a worker that has since lost its slice may
still land: the entry is what lets such a write be found and deleted.
Must exceed three times the command timeout of the store, plus the
clock difference between workers.

idle_timeout.description:
After this long without any record on a fully-read partition, its
watermark follows the wall clock so that downstream windows can close.

linger.description: Maximum time a source waits to fill a batch.

mailbox_capacity.description:
Capacity of every edge, in chunks. A full edge blocks its producer:
this is what propagates backpressure up to the source.

max_batch.description: Maximum number of source records per epoch (one KV commit per epoch).

max_in_flight_epochs.description: How many epochs a slice may have read but not yet committed.

max_out_of_orderness.description: Watermark = highest event time seen minus this bound.

max_pending_windows.description:
How many windows a slice may have closed, per aggregate, without their
results being emitted yet. Past that number the slice stops reading
until emission catches up: this is how a slow sink behind an aggregate
slows the sources down, and what bounds the state waiting in the store.
`0` removes the limit.

mostly waiting is limited by that system, not by this worker: more
